claims.statement: A named classical policy assigns planets to zodiac signs as domiciles or houses.
claims.scope: historical doctrine configuration, not astronomy fact

claims.statement: Ptolemy presents the domicile arrangement using a northern seasonal/natural-philosophy rationale together with planetary order and qualities.
claims.scope: what this primary text argues; not a scientific validation of astrology

claims.statement: Early-modern authors disagreed over whether season-dependent sign qualities and essential dignities should reverse in southern latitudes.
claims.scope: history of doctrine and applicability debate

claims.statement: In the reviewed modern classical-practitioner reference, domicile is framed as greater authority/capacity/resources and not as moral goodness.
claims.scope: one practitioner/reference framework; not project-canonical doctrine

conflict_groups.summary: Season-based rationale produced competing early-modern positions: reverse dignities in southern latitudes versus preserve standard dignities as universal and treat regional effects separately.
